records.title: A lesson is a rule
records.summary: What a run teaches is recorded as a rule with targets and a brief; only the brief reaches the targeted step, the body is read on demand.

records.title: Open questions are settled in grooming, not in develop
records.summary: Grooming hunts for open questions and settles them with the user before ready-for-dev; develop stops only for force majeure.

records.title: Every prompt artefact passes the information-architecture check
records.summary: Before a prompt-bearing artefact is saved, every block passes four checks — scoping, duplication, configurability, hierarchy — and prose that only restates or motivates is cut.

records.title: References a plan invalidates are cleaned up in the same sprint
records.summary: When a plan deletes or renames something others reference, the cleanup is a milestone task of the same sprint with its own DoD, never a follow-up sweep.

records.title: Generated content is scoped to its audience
records.summary: User-facing output — release notes, user docs, changelogs — includes only what that audience touches; the audience filter is specced into the task's DoD.

records.title: An agent briefing bounds what the agent returns
records.summary: Every agent briefing states the exact shape of the agent's reply, limited to what the orchestrator needs; groom bounds it in the task so develop's briefings inherit it.

records.title: The content of a user-facing output is locked in grooming
records.summary: When a plan defines a user-facing output or log format, its exact content — fields, truncation, trailers — is settled with the user in grooming, not iterated in develop.

records.title: Planning shows the values in play and every departure from them
records.summary: A plan names the values that drive its choices and flags where it departs from a value or rule, so the user sees what works and can refine the values.

records.title: Corrections are logged as they happen
records.summary: When the user corrects the driver, it logs the correction verbatim as a file under the vault's corrections/, so retro starts from a ready list of what is not yet handled.

records.title: Decisions are asked in prose
records.summary: An approval, or any decision the user must understand the context to make, is asked in prose, one at a time with compact context and a counter; a multiple-choice tool only for mechanical picks.

records.title: Decisions are listed for acceptance
records.summary: Before the user accepts anything, the agent lists every decision it takes as settled, one numbered line each, marking its own proposals; an unanswered item is never accepted.

records.title: A specs review tests each record against its type
records.summary: A review of the specs puts every record to the type tests of the format guide and lists each failure — the type it fits or deletion — for the user to accept.

records.title: Items of one class are groomed together, never in parallel
records.summary: The manager grooms items of the same class in one plan, or one after another with the earlier plan in the next brief — never in parallel, where each builds its own copy of the mechanism.

records.title: An ADR is accepted after a brief
records.summary: An ADR is drafted proposed and accepted only after the owner was shown its brief and given a window to object; the answer sets the review level with its evidence.

records.title: Open items hold only what outlives the session
records.summary: An open item is filed only for work for later or a question that waits for the owner; session instructions, gate answers, policies and decisions are never items.

records.title: Ids in chat carry their title
records.summary: Every id said in chat — an open item, an ADR, a rule, a plan — is followed by its short title; newly filed items are listed one per line with their title.

records.title: Experiments run in stages
records.summary: An experiment, eval or benchmark matrix runs a cheap screen, then a shortlist, then significance for finalists only, each stage sized before launch.

records.title: The ADR scorer judges its prompt alone
records.summary: The adr-scorer runs only its body render and judges a draft ADR from the pasted parts alone; nothing it was not shown exists for it.

records.title: The manager delegates heavy reads
records.summary: The project manager never reviews an artefact, reads a long file or scans many files or logs itself; a subagent does it under a bounded return contract and the manager keeps only the verdict.
records.review_evidence: owner, 2026-10-20: «Ты project manager, а не team lead или researcher, ты должен был это делегировать, очевидно, запиши… core правила, что project manager делегирует.»

records.title: Specs are a core feature in three tiers
records.summary: Booping ships the specs format and its own specs; a global tier in the home dir and a project tier in the repo add their records, cross-tier refs go by namespace.

records.title: Procedures are playbooks behind one skill
records.summary: Every booping procedure ships as a playbook driven by the single /playbook skill; a new skill is written only for a surface /playbook cannot drive.

records.title: Bodies render at skill load, with no build stage
records.summary: Skill and agent bodies are rendered from templates at load time with full project context; the generated-file build stage is retired.

records.title: Config is a three-tier deep merge with no schema gate
records.summary: Config merges core, global and project tiers, later winning and lists replacing; any key loads in any tier, and playbook keys live in the core file under core.{name}_playbook.

records.title: Each playbook owns its state machine; no shared lifecycle
records.summary: Every artifact moves only through its own playbook's states machine, written solely by playbook-transition; playbooks hand off at a status, not through a shared lifecycle.

records.title: Run-state persistence is an authored tier, and confirmation is a status
records.summary: A playbook's state machine is authored at one of three tiers — ephemeral, minimal, rich — never derived from the graph; a confirmation that must persist is a status transition, not a flag.

records.title: Retro and code review are separate tracks joined by plan frontmatter
records.summary: A plan ends at develop's done and never moves again; retro and code review keep their own artifacts and machines and join the plan through retro and code_reviews keys.

records.title: A plan is a directory whose index.md is both plan and run artifact
records.summary: A plan lives in plans/{slug}/; index.md is the plan document and the machine's artifact at once, and run sidecars sit beside it — no separate plan.md and no _runs/ workdir.

records.title: A milestone is a file handed to the worker by path
records.summary: Each milestone is its own file in its own directory with status and feedback beside it; develop hands a worker that file's path, never a slice of the plan body.

records.title: A step is inline, assisted or detached, set by one detached field
records.summary: The runner performs most steps itself; heavy reads go to a configured researcher that is resumed, not respawned; only a step that must not enter the runner's context is detached.

records.title: External agents and surfaces wire in through config; core names no external tool
records.summary: An external worker or review surface is a plain agent registered in config and steered by a targeted rule; core ships no wrapper for it and no playbook names it.

records.title: A playbook run stops for review at one gate
records.summary: Core playbooks take user decisions in-step and stop for approval once — groom at present, retro at synthesize, migrate before applying, develop only to confirm the branch.

records.title: Groom's cross-review is a detached step gated by one config key
records.summary: A second model reviews the drafted plan once, in its own detached step, only when core.groom_playbook.cross_review_agent names an agent; null skips the step.

records.title: Vault migrations ship with the plugin, keyed by a frontmatter id
records.summary: Migrations live in the plugin's migrations/ directory; the id in migration.md frontmatter is the only authority, and the .booping marker's latest_migration is the applied watermark.

records.title: Migrations apply strictly in sequence, one commit each, after one gate
records.summary: Migrate asks once over the whole pending set, then applies each migration in id order through a fresh sub-agent, advancing the watermark and committing before the next; a failure stops the run.

records.title: The task tracker is a best-effort mirror of the vault
records.summary: The vault stays authoritative; tracker hooks run in a separate CLI, absorb the tracker's failures with a warning, and booping-tracker sync reconciles by hand.

records.title: CLI behaviour is tested by a contract corpus, not by internal unit tests
records.summary: Each CLI subcommand is specified by language-neutral cases run through bin/booping; unit tests cover only algorithmic hotspots, and prose is owned by snapshots and mdcheck.

records.title: Prompt behaviour is checked by per-step eval suites, advisory and outside CI
records.summary: Each playbook step can carry a promptfoo suite with a deterministic smoke tier and a judged regress tier; runs are proposed, not launched by steps, and post an advisory PR comment.

records.title: Develop groups milestones per worker by story points, not by count
records.summary: Develop packs milestones per worker greedily within one wave under a max_sp cap of 15 instead of max_milestones_per_agent, and sp ≥ 5 is a hard groom gate.

records.title: The specs playbook is a guide, not a menu of actions
records.summary: One specs playbook explains every record type and principle plus the user's typical scenarios, and the model works out from the dialogue what to do.

records.title: Open items are a stored index; closed ones are filtered out
records.summary: Every gap between specs and code, open question or conflict is an open item stored in the vault and listed by an explicit command; closed items stay and are filtered.

records.title: Corrections are logged where they happen
records.summary: Each time the user corrects the model in groom, develop or code-review, a short entry with a link back to the dialogue goes into the run's corrections sidecar — the feed retro and learn read.

records.title: Each project publishes its specs site on GitLab Pages, under one index
records.summary: A project whose vault is in its repo builds its specs site in CI to Pages; an index at the group's Pages root lists them, rebuilt on a schedule from the projects that carry a topic.

records.title: Groom drafts the whole plan in one staged pass
records.summary: Groom is the plan template plus research then draft (V3a), no self-review step, without the 16 rules the model follows unprompted; the draft is one file.

records.title: A script cuts the drafted plan into milestone files
records.summary: The script `booping plan split` cuts the one-file plan on its milestone headings, byte for byte, into index.md and the milestone files; a model splits only what the script flags.

records.title: The owner reviews specs on the site and hands the review to an agent
records.summary: A review panel beside each record collects comments and a reviewed mark in the browser; an Outbox page shows and copies everything for the agent, which edits the records.

records.title: Playbooks consult the specs through a subagent
records.summary: A read-only subagent tells playbooks what the specs already decide, contradict or leave open.

records.title: Every playbook carries a base guidance on the specs
records.summary: Every playbook knows what the specs are, the values, and that it reads and writes them through a subagent, applying them where they raise quality; no per-playbook scenarios.

records.title: Groom has no separate review step
records.summary: A fresh Opus review lifts plan quality but adds about 10 minutes a plan (4–5 at best); the one-pass draft already meets the goal, so groom has no review step.

records.title: Autonomy is settled in prose
records.summary: A run is autonomous because the user or its launch prompt says so, not because a config key does; there is no core.autonomy.

records.title: Journal entries are vault files built from existing primitives
records.summary: A correction or an agent decision is one vault file with frontmatter, made by create, moved by frontmatter-update and sliced by query; an item's question is its clarify status; no journal command.

records.title: Milestone shape is an mdcheck schema
records.summary: Groom checks each milestone file with mdcheck against a schema in the groom playbook; `booping plan check` and its code go, and mdcheck becomes a required dependency.

records.title: A session in a booping project starts pointed at the playbooks
records.summary: In a project with a .booping marker a SessionStart hook injects when to use playbooks and the rendered playbook table; the agent offers the fitting one, the manager by default.
records.review_evidence: «Давай opus сразу… В остальном, да, все правильно» — 2026-10-19, chat (plan + ADR briefs)

records.title: Records carry a review level with evidence
records.summary: A spec record's review is its own axis beside status — none, shown, discussed, accepted — and accepted carries the owner's words and where they were said; it replaces the reviewed date.
records.review_evidence: «Давай opus сразу… В остальном, да, все правильно» — 2026-10-19, chat (plan + ADR briefs)

records.title: The ADR scorer reads the specs guide and the tier's record inventory
records.summary: The adr-scorer gets the specs guide excerpt, the tier's value/rule/ADR inventory and the project's primitives, on Opus without tools, and answers route, overlaps, alt_score and missing.
records.review_evidence: «С, очевидно, надо брать» … «Ну все газ, вроде ок все» — 2026-10-19, chat

records.title: Every request in a booping session enters through the project-manager
records.summary: Every request in a booping project session, questions and debugging included, goes to the project-manager, which routes it and launches and orchestrates the other playbooks.

records.title: Plans run to the end ↔ Adjustable control
records.summary: An agent that carries a plan to the end on its own pulls against a human who can review deeply and take control back; the run's autonomy mode settles which applies.

records.title: Effective human review ↔ Plans run to the end ↔ Quality at a rational cost
records.summary: More review checkpoints make review effective but cost run time and stops; core playbooks stop for review once, and groom runs no separate review step.

records.title: Groom offers past plans and retros as context before planning
records.summary: Before planning, groom has a cheap researcher list past plans and retros related to the request, and reads the ones the user picks in depth.

records.title: Learn prefers guidance to validators
records.summary: Learn should propose guidance that steers a step away from an issue, and propose a validator or sub-agent check only for critical cases.

records.title: A faster groom without losing quality
records.summary: Try several groom playbook variants and keep the one that runs faster with no loss in plan quality.

records.title: Trim template fields that do not help
records.summary: Drop the business-goal logic from grooming and replace the retro action table's Owner column with "when to do it".

records.title: Booping as a web service with thin skills
records.summary: A web service owns playbook management, artefacts and execution; skills become thin clients, a tracker such as Linear is a driver, and a sandbox runs the workers.

records.title: Merged OSS PRs as benchmark tasks
records.summary: Re-create small merged PRs from OSS repos as booping plans and score groom and develop by the repo's own tests.

records.title: Claude wires a worker agent into booping on request
records.summary: The user asks Claude Code to add a native agent or a CLI-backed agent to a playbook, and Claude writes the agent, the config entry and the targeted rule.

records.title: Plans draft ADRs for their real forks
records.summary: Where a plan meets a real design fork, groom writes an ADR draft with the alternatives and its choice, and offers it to the owner for review unless the run is autonomous.

records.title: Groom depth scales with the task
records.summary: A small, already-decided request takes a light path to develop instead of a full groom, and groom runs its deeper work only when the task or the user asks for it.

records.title: Audience
records.summary: Booping is read by three roles — users, advanced users and contributors — each coming for different things at a different depth, in a different voice.

records.title: Glossary
records.summary: The canonical names for booping's concepts — one term per concept, never a synonym, used across records, docs and step bodies.

records.title: Documentation surfaces
records.summary: Booping's markdown documentation surfaces, each with its audience and the depth ceiling past which content belongs elsewhere; executed or generated markdown is not a surface.

records.title: Develop model comparison, April 2026
records.summary: One develop diff each from Claude Opus 4.7, Minimax 2.7 and GLM 5.1 scored 9.7, 7.2 and 6.4 of 10; only Opus produced a correct, plan-compliant diff.

records.title: Bench finding — develop follows the plan's code sketch over a lesson
records.summary: In claude-booping-bench, /develop copied the casing of the plan's code sketch instead of a loaded naming lesson in 3 of 3 reps (judgment 0.2).

records.title: Groom cost — playbook versus the old skill
records.summary: On one measured request the playbook groom took 2.4× the wall time, 5.2× the main-thread API calls and 3.0× the output tokens of the old /groom skill.

records.title: Groom benchmark 2026-10 — variants, rule ablation, plan split
records.summary: What the October 2026 groom benchmark measured, what the model does without being told, what it cost and where the data lives.

records.title: Postmortem: the budget gate slipped into the core unasked
records.summary: On 2026-10-15 a usage-limit gate the owner never asked for reached the core through a one-line mention, a package approval and autonomous runs; removed on 2026-10-17.

records.title: Prose or code probes 2026-10
records.summary: Three cheap probes on 2026-10-18 — which rule wording makes a fresh model pick prose, an existing primitive or a new CLI correctly, and how sibling items should be groomed.

records.title: Postmortem: mechanisms built without a reader
records.summary: Between 2026-10-15 and 2026-10-18 booping grew a config key and three journal CLIs that nothing needed; removed on 2026-10-18, with the rule wording and the ADR guide that let them in.

records.title: Postmortem: CLI commands removed under live runs
records.summary: On 2026-10-17/18 booping removed the budget, correction and defaults commands while autonomous runs in another project still called them, and those runs failed.

records.title: What is not in the source is marked, not invented
records.summary: A record or artefact states only what its source says; an open point is marked [clarify] or "not named in the source", never filled in by the agent.

records.title: The compact artefact is reviewed before the detail
records.summary: Where a human reviews, a run first produces a compact artefact the human can read and reorder, and builds the expensive detail only on the reviewed one.

records.title: Every step ends by naming the next one
records.summary: A playbook step or a run that hands back to the user ends by naming the next step and how to call it; a premature call says what is missing.

records.title: Every diff is reviewed in Plannotator, never in chat
records.summary: In this project the code-review human step always runs through the plannotator-reviewer agent; a missing agent or a dead surface stops the run, never falls back to chat.

records.title: Snapshot baselines are accepted by the user, never by a run
records.summary: A run never runs just snapshots-accept or writes the committed playbook reports; it leaves the drift uncommitted and names it in its final report for the user to accept.

records.title: Code review covers code files only
records.summary: A code review surfaces findings on code files only; documentation, plans and other prose in the diff pass unreviewed.

records.title: Structured data is rendered from config, never restated in prose
records.summary: Statuses, queues, agent ids, globs and other structured values live in config or query specs and are rendered into bodies; prose never copies a literal.

records.title: Project specifics stay out of the core
records.summary: Core skills and playbooks stay stack-agnostic; whatever is specific to a project is written into that project's tier, never into the core or a user-level scope by a run.

records.title: The driver owns the vault and git; workers touch only repo code
records.summary: The driver owns the vault, run state and commits; workers edit only repo code, never git history; a small fix goes to the session already holding its context.

records.title: Project shaping of an agent or skill is a targeted record
records.summary: A project adjusts a core agent or skill through a targeted rule (agent:<id>, skill:<name>), never through a separate extension file.

records.title: Commits are conventional with a scope
records.summary: Commit messages follow Conventional Commits with a scope, such as feat(booping) or fix(groom).

records.title: The README Statuses section follows the states blocks
records.summary: The README's Statuses section is a hand-kept narrative over each playbook's states block; a change to a states block revisits it in the same change.

records.title: A new procedure is a playbook, not a skill
records.summary: Anything procedural is added as a playbook driven by /playbook; a new skill is added only for a surface /playbook cannot drive.

records.title: Who reads the result decides prose or code
records.summary: A command, key or check exists when code reads its result or it supplies a fact the model cannot see; the rest is prose, the default when unsure.

records.title: Step bodies are fetched on demand, not pasted into spawn prompts
records.summary: A step's body is fetched when the step runs rather than pasted into a spawn prompt, so a run's context grows with its graph, not with the sum of its step bodies.

records.title: A hermetic render repeats byte for byte
records.summary: With macros stubbed and the config merge pinned to core and project levels, a render is identical on any machine.

records.title: Vault artefacts are plain markdown with YAML frontmatter
records.summary: Every artefact a run writes into the project vault is plain markdown with YAML frontmatter, readable in Obsidian.

records.title: Graph and render problems are reported in band, never as crashes
records.summary: A graph or render problem surfaces as a STOP or Note notice in the rendered output at exit 0, never as a crash.

records.title: A prompt rule earns its place by a measured miss
records.summary: An instruction enters a prompt or a targeted rule only after a minimal probe shows the model missing it; evals and benchmarks run only when the owner agrees.

records.title: Judgement runs on Opus; cheaper models only for routine with a known output
records.summary: Every step, agent or fallback that decides — drafts, reviews, verifies a DoD, writes tests — runs on Opus; the researcher on Sonnet high; else only mechanical steps.

records.title: The booping CLI holds only generic primitives
records.summary: A booping CLI command is a primitive any playbook can use; behaviour of one playbook's domain is that playbook's script, run through its hooks.

records.title: Private sources stay in vault/notes
records.summary: This repo is public; another project's data, local paths and raw experiment inputs are written only under the gitignored vault/notes/, and tracked records name them without linking.

records.title: Cut a plugin release
records.summary: A release is a release/X.Y.Z branch bumping plugin.json and CHANGELOG.md, merged by PR into master, then tagged vX.Y.Z with a GitHub release on the merge commit.

records.title: Run the eval suites and read the PR comment
records.summary: Evals run locally on subscription auth via just smoke/regress/eval; results land as one sticky advisory PR comment, never a gate.

records.title: Accept new snapshot and contract baselines
records.summary: After an intentional change, the user reads the snapshot or txtar drift and accepts it; a run or a worker never accepts a baseline itself.

records.title: Playbook driver
records.summary: The /playbook skill discovers a procedure across the core, global and project levels and drives it to completion.

records.title: Run state machines
records.summary: A run's state lives in per-playbook states: machines that only the booping CLI advances.

records.title: Layered configuration
records.summary: Config is a deep merge over the core, global and project levels, and any mapping in it can be a query spec or a template tree.

records.title: Targeted rules
records.summary: An accepted rule's brief is injected into exactly the playbooks, steps, agents or skills its targets: list names.

records.title: Plan and review templates
records.summary: Groom and code-review offer plan and review templates the user authored in the Project Vault or at the global level.

records.title: User playbooks
records.summary: Playbooks the user authors at the global level or in the Project Vault are discovered and run beside the core ones.

records.title: External agents
records.summary: Agents the plugin does not ship are wired into playbook agent slots through config and shaped per project by targeted rules.

records.title: Template pipeline
records.summary: Skill and agent bodies render in one runtime stage from src/templates/ with full project context, reproducibly when pinned.

records.title: Quality gates
records.summary: just ci runs lint, typecheck, pytest, snapshots, mdcheck and e2e in order, holding the plugin's behaviour.

records.title: pytest-txtar
records.summary: The e2e corpus's case format and sandboxed runner ship as a standalone pytest plugin on PyPI.

records.title: Eval suites
records.summary: Promptfoo suites beside each step guard its contract in a deterministic and an llm-rubric tier.

records.title: Migration shipping
records.summary: The plugin ships Project Vault migrations, and every render surface is gated on a vault's applied watermark.

records.title: Documentation site
records.summary: The public MkDocs reference builds strictly and publishes to gh-pages on push to master.

records.title: Project setup
records.summary: The setup playbook takes a repo from any state to a working booping project and re-runs without changing what is already set up.

records.title: Project Vault migrations
records.summary: The migrate playbook brings an existing Project Vault current with the plugin on one up-front approval, with one commit per migration.

records.title: Groom
records.summary: Groom shapes a feature, bug or refactor into a specified, estimated plan the user approved, ending at ready-for-dev.

records.title: Develop
records.summary: Develop executes a groomed plan one milestone group at a time through a worker agent and closes it at done or fail.

records.title: Retro
records.summary: Retro mines a finished sprint's session logs, diff and the user's feedback into a standalone retrospective.

records.title: Learn
records.summary: Learn turns retrospective findings the user confirmed into rule records in the project specs tier or CLAUDE.md entries.

records.title: Session metrics
records.summary: A plan carries measured active minutes, tokens and models computed from Claude Code session logs.

records.title: Code review
records.summary: The code-review playbook reviews a confirmed scope, collects the human verdict and applies only approved fixes.

records.title: Task tracker
records.summary: The booping-tracker CLI carries every interaction with an issue tracker, and groom mirrors its run status and questions onto the tracker issue.

records.title: Project manager
records.summary: One manager the user talks to files every request as an item and carries it through groom, develop, review and merge, with a status computed from the vault.

records.title: Specs review with the owner
records.summary: The system reviews the owner's specs, fixes what is plainly stale, and brings the owner only the decisions that are theirs, one at a time and kept across restarts.

records.title: Own integration on top of booping
records.summary: An advanced user wires their own triggers, schedules, tracker flows and usage guards on top of booping's surfaces; the core ships none of them.

records.title: Specs first, then code
records.summary: A decision made in the specs becomes tracked work the code follows, closed with its plan; code that ran ahead of the specs becomes work for the specs.

records.title: Curated self-learning
records.summary: The system gets better from its own runs, but only through the user and when the user wants it: a lesson becomes a rule after the user takes it, not after every run.

records.title: Minimal effective context
records.summary: A step gets only what it needs.

records.title: Single source
records.summary: Each fact, decision and piece of structured data lives in one place and is referenced or rendered from there; a decision is kept together with its reason.

records.title: Analysable history
records.summary: Plans, runs and their outcomes are kept across every project, so the history can be analysed: practices taken over from one project to another, benchmarks, quality comparison, problem analysis.

records.title: Stack-agnostic core
records.summary: The core knows nothing about a stack or a project; specifics live in the global and the project tiers.

records.title: A framework for playbooks
records.summary: Booping is a framework a user digitises their own processes with — config, templates, primitives, the CLI, playbooks and evals for their steps.

records.title: Plans run to the end
records.summary: The agent carries a plan through to the end on its own unless force majeure stops it.

records.title: Effective human review
records.summary: Every step where a human takes part is convenient and effective for that human.

records.title: Adjustable control
records.summary: The human can review the system deeply, or give the agent more freedom to act inside the values and boundaries.

records.title: Proven to work
records.summary: We know the system works as it should and can guarantee it high enough to call it reliable.

records.title: Everything in one place
records.summary: Everything is plain files, easy to look at from one place — for example Obsidian; symlinks back to the project repos keep it together.

records.title: Quality at a rational cost
records.summary: Booping is a work tool for professionals, so the quality of the result matters.

records.title: Guides to the goal
records.summary: The system is clear to the user and leads them to the goal by the hand, while letting a professional step aside and get there their own way.

records.title: Comfort for non-technical users
records.summary: How comfortable booping is for people without a strong technical background is not optimised for; they are not its audience.

records.title: Deterministic where code reads it
records.summary: What code reads, and every fact outside the model's view, is produced by code; what only a model or a human reads stays prose with a fixed format until code starts to read it.

records.title: Specs live with the work
records.summary: Specs are updated as the work happens and applied wherever they raise the quality of a result; they never go stale or depend on the user remembering them.

records.title: Launching and guarding runs is userland
records.summary: When and how development runs start — triggers, schedules, tracker and messenger integrations — and guarding usage limits are the user's, not booping's; booping offers an integration surface at most.

records.title: A core set for development and self-learning
records.summary: On top of the framework booping ships core playbooks for development, self-learning among them; they are its dogfooding, built only from mechanics a user playbook gets too.

records.title: Projects are built along a roadmap
records.summary: Work decomposes into plans and sprints, so a project is written along its roadmap, sprint by sprint, with a manager carrying the work through.
